1. This criminal petition arises out of the complaint filed by the 2nd respondent, on the basis of which a crime was registered in Crime No.137/2023 of Kumata Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 of the IPC, 1860 and 66(D) of IT Act, 2000.
2. Both parties along with the learned counsel representing the respective parties are present.
3. Today, the learned counsel for the petitioner has filed a joint memo for compounding the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 of the IPC, 1860 and 66(D) of IT Act, 2000.

The joint memo reads as under:
"JOINT MEMO FILED UNDER SECTION 320(6) & (8) OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE CODE Herein the advocate for the petitioner / accused and complainant / respondent no. 2 submits before this Hon'ble Court as follows;
This compromise deed has been entered into between the petitioner / accused and complainant / respondent no. 2 on the following terms and conditions:-
1. That the respondent no.2 i.e. complainant had got lodged an FIR No. 137/2023 registered U/s 419/420 of NC: 2024:KHC-D:854 the Indian Penal Code, 1860 & 66D IT Act, 2000 at Police Station Kumta, District Uttar Kannada, Karnataka against the petitioner.
2. That now the friends and respectable of the society qua both the parties have got the matter compromised between the petitioner / accused and complainant /
respondent no. 2 and there remains no grudge against each other between the same.
3. That the respondent no.2 i.e., Complainant has received the entire amount from the petitioner and now nothing is due towards the petitioner.

sentences.text: That the compromise has been affected between the petitioner and respondent no.2 in order to keep harmony and brotherhood in the society.

Now the respondent no.2 i.e., Complainant does not want to pursue the above said FIR against the petitioner or his officer bearer/staff and further shall be having no objection if the above said FIR is cancelled/quashed by Hon'ble High Court.

The respondent no.2 i.e., Complainant undertakes that if the statement of the respondent no.2 is required for the cancellation of the above said FIR in any competent court, then respondent No.2 will make the statement in the competent court and further have no objection if the petitioner i.e., accused will be discharged/acquitted in the above said case.

5. That the present compromise has been affected between the petitioner and respondent no.2 without any NC: 2024:KHC-D:854 pressure, undue influence and with their free mind and will.
6. That from today no party shall take any action or will not file any case for damages or claim for imputation of the reputation and also not move for any civil or criminal litigation against each other.
Hence it is just and necessary to permit the petitioner and the respondent no: 2 to compound the said case instead of subjecting the petitioners to face the trial.

HEREFORE, the petitioner & respondent no. 2 humbly prays before this Hon'ble Court that the petition as prayed by the petitioner may be allowed in terms of compromise, in the ends of justice."
4.

Having regard to the nature of the complaint and in the light of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh vs State Of Punjab & Anr reported in 2012(10) SCC 303 there would be no impediment to permit the petitioner to compound the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 of the IPC, 1860 and 66(D) of IT Act, 2000.

sentences.text: Consequently, the proceedings initiated against the petitioner/accused stands quashed.

5. If the bank accounts of the petitioner/accused are frozen as a result of these proceedings, the authorities shall NC: 2024:KHC-D:854 take steps to de-freeze the bank accounts of the petitioner/accused.
